subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a futuristic militarized truck design, structuring it with a chassis root, suspension joints, wheel spin joints, and turret yaw/pitch, aiming for a rich but manageable part count around 200 pieces with cyberpunk-style textures.

I'm working out the dimensions and helper functions for the truck geometry, deciding on paint and color schemes using gunmetal tones with wear and dirt effects, and sketching out the overall design featuring an armored wedge cab, missile pod launcher, turret, neon light bar, and armored hexagonal wheels.

I'm adding decal details like hazard stripes, an invented militia logo, numbers, and glyphs, then setting up precise hub and wheel joint coordinates so the spin animation rotates correctly about the right axis.

Now I'm building the chassis using boxes and extrusions for angled panels, sketching out a cab profile outline with a raked windscreen defined as a polygon of z,y points to extrude into the body shape.

I'm checking that the hull doesn't clip through the wheels given their radius and position, so I'm adjusting the hull thickness and adding separate fender boxes to cover the wheel width properly.

For the windscreen, I'm figuring out a tilted glass panel using a rotated box positioned at the slope between the hood and roof, calculating the diagonal length and rotation angle needed so it sits flush against the frame.

Working out the side window geometry next, defining quad profiles for the glass panels along the hull edges and figuring where the roofline meets the side slopes.

The protrusion is small enough to accept, so I'll color the glass dark teal without glow and add a HUD decal. For the doors, I'm setting up hinge joints at the front edge with armor plate boxes overlapping the hull slightly as proud surface detail, leaving windows on the hull separate. Now I'm moving on to building the bed with floor and rail side boxes.

Building wheels...

Now I'm planning the suspension setup with arm rods, torus coil springs, and shock mounts per wheel, then moving on to hull paint with a gunmetal base, lighter highlights up top, dirt accumulation near the bottom, and panel line detailing.

For the paint variants I'm defining a cyberpunk palette—gunmetal, hazard yellow, neon cyan, magenta, warning orange—plus a mottled dark teal accent for armor plates. Then I'm sketching out a texture list, starting with hazard stripe diagonals applied via plane geometry on the bumper edges, followed by a corporate logo decal.

I'm planning more textures: a unit/door number stencil, HUD windscreen glass, geometric glyph panels in place of risky font-rendered kanji, a scrolling LED pixel grid for the taillight, a barcode serial plate, a glowing circuit trace pattern for the side skirts, and a radar scan screen.

Now I'm working out the plane geometry and orientation logic for side panels, making sure textures face outward correctly depending on which side they're on, and noting that glow effects only apply safely to flat, untextured parts.

Layout-wise I'm planning the turret assembly with yaw and pitch joints on the roof, barrels, sensor ball, and ammo boxes, then moving to the rear VLS bed with angled hex tubes, a hinged lid, and eight glowing cells inside.

For the VLS cells, I'm considering torus rims with a magenta glow and cone-shaped missile heads, but deciding to skip an actual elevation pose for the launcher and just keep it level with the box raised slightly for simplicity. I'm also planning the bed walls as sloped side plates with a floor, plus a rear tailgate with a hinge joint and a tail LED strip.

Now I'm working out fenders as wheel arch boxes positioned above each wheel with accent coloring, plus a lower chassis frame beneath the main hull for ground clearance, and checking the overall truck height adds up to roughly 3 meters once the turret and antennas are factored in.

Checking the 12-block tread arrangement confirms the lowest block sits at y≈-0.01, within tolerance. Now I'm working out the skirt panels between the wheels, sizing them relative to the hull width, and planning a neon underglow strip plus circuit-pattern texture along the sides for visual detail.

For the front end, I'm sketching a wedge-shaped ram bumper using a frustum shape tapering along the z-axis, adding spikes, a winch, hazard decals, hexagonal glowing grille slats, and headlights, while also planning glowing mirror camera pods, an alternating cyan/magenta roof light bar, antennas with a rotating radar spinner joint.

Now I'm detailing more features: split left/right headlight boxes with amber turn lamps, ERA tile armor on the hood made of a 4x3 grid of boxes, orange vent strips, A-pillar camera pods, and various decals including a door emblem, hood unit number, bed serial, hazard markings, a windscreen HUD, and a pixel-style rear tail LED display. I'm also considering adding jerrycans, a spare tire, and other side details to push the intricacy further.

Thinking through more additions like smoke discharger banks on the cab sides, cable bundles swept along the bed, exhaust stacks with glowing tips at the cab rear, and a sensor dome, then I'm planning the joint skeleton—chassis, suspension, wheels, yaw/pitch, doors, tailgate, VLS lid, radar—keeping it to roughly 20 joints with a hinge-based suspension travel joint parenting the wheel joints.

Now I'm making sure every joint explicitly declares its parent rather than relying on defaults, with chassis as the root joint, and starting to write SVG texture strings for the hazard stripe pattern and the KRYO logo with its hexagon outline and stylized lettering.

Writing import statements...

I'll keep imports lean to avoid unused-import errors, then set up the color palette and start defining the hull paint function with gradient and dirt-weathering effects.

Writing paint layers...

Defining the chassis joint...

Building out the frame rails, cross members, belly plate, and battery packs with cyan glow strips for that cyberpunk EV look, keeping wheel clearance in mind.

Writing hull extrude code...

I'm working out the windscreen geometry by calculating the slope angle between the roof point and hood point, then figuring out the rotation needed to align a glass box along that tilted axis.

Now I'm computing the normal vector for the glass face so it angles outward correctly, and sizing it to fit within the hull width minus frame margins. I'm considering using a textured plane instead of a box for the windscreen, positioned slightly offset along its normal.

Next I'm planning the side windows as extruded panels at the hull's sides, the raised roof plate with panel details, and a rear headboard box for the bed area, plus thinking through where to place a roof-mounted sensor mast or turret.

Now I'm positioning the roof boundaries, adding a front light bar with alternating glowing cyan/magenta strips, and working out door geometry — hinge joints, panel dimensions, and window cutout placement along the hull.

Adding door details and wheel arches...

Working out wheel well clearance against the bed floor and side walls so the wheels tuck in cleanly, then planning segmented skirt plates with glowing circuit textures along the sides, and starting on the front grille placement set into the hull's sloped nose face.

Placing headlight glow boxes near the nose, adding horizontal grille slats tinted magenta, and sketching a vertical bumper frustum shape at the front.

Adding chassis-colored spikes and rods using the bone helper functions for the frame details, then planning a hazard texture plane near the bumper.

I'm also working out the bumper and bed geometry dimensions—positioning the front bumper face, sizing the hazard stripe plane, and laying out the truck bed floor box and side wall extrusion profile.

Now I'm shaping the tailgate slope profile and sizing the armor thickness, then placing a headboard panel behind the cab and setting up the VLS launcher box position with its cell grid dimensions.

Working out the 12-cell VLS grid with dark cylinders and glowing rings per cell, adding silver missile caps to a couple cells, and designing a single hinged hatch panel to cover the rear row of launch tubes.

I'm adjusting the VLS box dimensions and wall heights to fit flush against the chassis, then adding a hinged tailgate panel with a red LED strip, corner taillights, and a textured "2077" display plane on the rear.

Now I'm placing the rear bumper and figuring out the exhaust stack positions behind the cab, adjusting their height range to clear the headboard.

I'm also adding a glowing exhaust tip with a perforated heat shield, plus angled smoke discharger tubes mounted at the cab's roof corners, then moving on to the mirrors.

Mirror stalks and boxes attach near the cab front, including a camera glow lens detail. Now I'm setting up the remote weapons station turret with yaw and pitch joints, defining the torus ring base, drum cylinder, and housing box components on the chassis and yaw layers.

Continuing the turret build I'm laying out cheek plates, ammo boxes, the cradle, twin barrel rods with shrouds, muzzle brakes, sensor pod, and an electro-optic ball sphere.

I'm adding a radar pole and rotating antenna joint on the rear roof, whip antennas tilted from the roof corners, and now placing A-pillar camera pods and ERA bricks across the hood slope.

Calculating hood surface angle...

Now I'm laying out hood detail bricks in a grid, spacing them across four columns and three rows, with alternating accent and dark metal colors while leaving the center open for a glowing vent strip.

Skipping the front nose wedge for now. For the cargo bed I'll add glowing cable harness sweeps connecting the VLS box to the cab, a roof light bar with alternating cyan/magenta segments, and underglow strips along the sides in cyan.

For wheels, I'm setting up a per-wheel function handling joints and suspension—arm rods from chassis to hub, upper arm connections, and a simplified coil spring built from stacked tori following the axis direction.

For steering, I'm adding front steer joints (chassis→suspension→steer→wheel chain with hinge directions) while rear wheels connect directly to suspension. Wheel parts include the tire cylinder with rotation, tread details, and rim.

Still building wheel components...

Now I'm planning hazard stripe SVG textures using yellow and black polygons on a dark background.

For the logo, I'm designing a circular emblem with a cyan ring, a magenta hexagonal outline, and a bold yellow lightning-bolt-like path, plus text near the bottom edge.

For the unit badge, I'm sketching a small rounded rectangle with a dark fill and cyan border, bold "MIL-77" text, and stroke widths scaled so they stay crisp at render size.

For the HUD element, I'm laying out a windscreen rectangle with a dark teal gradient, faint cyan scan lines, a central reticle circle, and tiny telemetry text like "SPD 000".

I'm making sure any semi-transparent reflective overlays sit on top of a fully opaque background rect so they don't get clipped by transparency rules, then adding circuit-trace glow textures for the skirts, a small red tail display showing "2077," and a yellow serial plate with black "KR-2077-X" text and rivet details for the tailgate.

I'm rounding out the texture list with a warning label for the missile bay reading "DANGER // AMMO" alongside a triangle-and-exclamation icon, giving eight total textures (hazard, logo, unit marking, HUD, circuit, tail, plate, warning), and setting up glow intensities for the logo and circuit/tail displays so they read as neon against the body panels.

Adding more panel details...

Bumper height checks out fine for the export. I'm setting up helper functions for symmetry pairs, spikes, rods, and coils to build out the greebled parts efficiently.

Now I'm working through placement details: hood slope at 7°, door joints that swing as boxes, and positioning the radar arm bone so it clears the roof turret and light bar without overlapping. Skipping the dish detail and moving to write the final code.
